resources.string: Get readings straight from a Dexcom G7 or ONE+ sensor over Bluetooth. No Dexcom app or xDrip is needed. Pair the sensor with the code on its applicator.
Needed to find the sensor and to receive its readings.
AAPS will stop reading this sensor and forget its key. The sensor keeps its phone slot for this phone for about 15 minutes. To use it with another app, wait that long first.
Paired. Waiting for the first reading (can take 5 minutes)
Sensor expired. Readings go on for up to 12 hours. Replace the sensor.
Sensor session ended. Apply and pair a new sensor.
Sensor failed. Remove it and start a new sensor. Check your glucose with a meter.
Bluetooth is off or not allowed
Press \"Pair new sensor\" and scan the applicator
The sensor is used by another phone or app. A sensor works with one phone app at a time. Stop the other app from using this sensor, then wait 15 minutes.
The sensor refused this phone\'s key. Pair the sensor again.
The sensor does not match the stored pairing code. Pair the sensor again.
The sensor refused the connection. AAPS tries again in 15 minutes.

The sensor is calibrated in the factory. Only calibrate when readings are clearly wrong. Wash your hands, use a fresh meter reading, and do not calibrate while glucose changes fast. The value goes to the sensor at its next reading.
A calibration can only be sent to a sensor that is running normally (not in warmup, expired or failed).
%1$s entered at %2$s, waiting for the sensor
%1$s accepted at %2$s, the sensor is still applying it
These apps are installed: %1$s. A sensor works with one phone app at a time. Make sure they do not use this sensor, or uninstall them.
The current sensor will be replaced by the new one.
1. Keep the applicator: its barcode or 4-digit code is needed for pairing.
2. Apply the sensor to the back of your upper arm, as the Dexcom instructions say.
3. Keep the phone close to the sensor during pairing. Android may ask to pair with the sensor: accept it.
4. After pairing, the sensor warms up for about 30 minutes (up to an hour for 15-day sensors). Readings come every 5 minutes.
Scan the barcode on the applicator, or type the 4-digit pairing code printed on it.
Point the camera at the square barcode on the applicator.
This barcode does not look like a Dexcom product. Check the code.
This barcode has no pairing code. Scan the barcode on the applicator.
A sensor used by another phone in the last 15 minutes can take up to 20 minutes to be found.
The first reading comes within 5 minutes. A new sensor warms up first.
The pairing code is the 4-digit number printed on the applicator.
Bluetooth is off or not allowed. Turn it on and allow AAPS to use it.
No sensor was found. Make sure the sensor is applied, the phone is close to it, and no other phone or app uses it.
Could not pair with any sensor in range. Check the code.
Dexcom G7: the sensor ends in about 24 hours. Have a new sensor ready.
Dexcom G7: the sensor ends in about 2 hours. Change it soon to avoid a gap in readings.
Dexcom G7: the sensor has expired. Readings go on for up to 12 hours. Replace it before then.
Dexcom G7: the sensor session has ended and readings have stopped. Apply and pair a new sensor.
Dexcom G7: the sensor has failed and sends no usable readings. Remove it and start a new sensor. Check your glucose with a meter.
Dexcom G7: the sensor refused the connection. It may be used by another phone or app. Open Dexcom G7 Direct for details.
Dexcom G7: warmup finished, readings are in use.
